name: Khejri seed storage (cow dung, cow urine, ash)
description: Seeds washed with cow dung and cow urine, then stored in ash to prevent insect attacks (Part II p.4). The practitioner is not explicitly named.

name: Organic, low-water sweet potato varieties (Panchariya)
description: Organic sweet potato cultivation (Part I p.14); 'Eight varieties of sweet potatoes' (Part I p.15 caption); five varieties developed by selection over seven years, needing less water, some with deep red hue (Part II p.4).

name: Millet-based products (Panchariya)
description: Showcased by Rahulchand/Rawalchand Panchariya (Part I p.14; Part II p.2).

name: New carrot variety (Santosh Pachar)
description: Developed by Smt. Santosh Pachar (Part I p.14).

name: Apples grown in Rajasthan (variety originally developed by Hariman Sharma)
description: Sundaram Ji brought apples grown in Rajasthan of a variety originally developed by Hariman Sharma in Himachal Pradesh (Part I p.14).

name: Stainless-steel glass lending (Likhmidas Temple)
description: Steel glasses lent for events like marriages on condition that 20 per cent more glasses are returned, to reduce plastic glasses (Part I p.14).

name: Temple fundraising: 1 gaj of land for Rs 501 (Rs 1.80 crore in one day)
description: Likhmidas Temple received donations worth Rs 1.80 crore in one day by offering 1 gaj of temple land for Rs 501 (Part I p.14).

name: Kasuri Methi processing (Nagaur)
description: Selection, manual cleaning and grading of dried fenugreek leaves; Nagaur's water said to contribute to superior quality; UV-light suggestion; possible GI application discussed (Part I p.14).

name: Model of the solar system (Rajaram Tak)
description: Presented by teacher Rajaram Tak at Atusar (Part I p.14).

name: Greening homes with bonsai (Shravan Kumar Soni)
description: Demonstration of making home spaces greener with bonsai plants (Part I p.14).

name: Thigh-supported crutch (Kanaramji)
description: Crutch that supported his leg from the thigh, freeing his hands (Part I p.14).

name: Traditional animal remedies (Kanaramji)
description: Retained umbilical cord after calving: old bamboo ground, boiled in water, strained through cloth and given cooled; loose motion: isabgol soaked in cold water (Part II p.4).

name: Farming with camels (Sataram)
description: The only farmer in the village using camels for farming (Part I p.15).

name: Electric wheelchair (Dharamveer Khambojji)
description: Invention shown by Dharamveer Khambojji (Part I p.15).

name: Fruit juices (Dharamveer Khambojji)
description: Shown by Dharamveer Khambojji as his inventions (Part I p.15).

name: Scooter that starts only when the helmet is worn
description: Idea received in the idea competitions; linked URL https://nif.org.in/innovation/wear_a-helmet-to-start_your-two-wheeler/706 (Part I p.15). Innovator not named in the article.

name: Device indicating whether a field needs manure (Rinku Jeji)
description: Idea competition entry (Part I p.15).

name: Bottle with hot and cold water simultaneously (Simran)
description: Idea competition entry (Part I p.15).

name: Village study rooms with tables and A/Cs (Ram Chandra Sirohi)
description: Reflected in the number of academic toppers, most of them girls (Part II p.3).

name: Rudimentary robot by two school students
description: Made by two students in the 8th and 10th grade (Part II p.3); students not named.

name: Four tree types side by side so fruit is always available for birds and animals
description: Seen on some farms (Part II p.4); farmers not named.

name: Tractors from Rs 50,000 with flexible repayment (Ram Ratanji)
description: Part II p.4.

name: Sathika moth ki daal (Vigna aconitifolia / turkish gram)
description: Ready in 60 days, grows with only two or three rains; taste reportedly decreased; similar for moong dal (Part II p.4).

name: Ker (medicinal plant / delicacy)
description: Plucked from thorny trees; medicinal; costs around Rs 1800-2000/kg; a delicacy at marriages (Part I p.14).

name: Precision tools for jewellery-making (Loharpura blacksmiths)
description: ~500 blacksmith families; challenges: small coal furnaces, non-ergonomic positions, poorly ventilated workshops, inadequate eye protection (Part II p.3).

name: Paan methi cultivation (farmer not named)
description: Another farmer at Mundwa spoke of an innovative approach to cultivating paan methi (Part I p.15).
